entry.title: v1.6.6rc1 — History controls, connectors, and sync hardening
entry.content:
v1.6.6rc1 — History controls, connectors, and sync hardening

Release Date: 2026-10-23
Changes: v1.6.5.dev0 → v1.6.6rc1

Pull Requests: #5765, #5850, #5893, #5898, #5938, #5955, #5958, #5961, #6011, #6013, #6014, #6185

Summary

This release focuses on giving users clearer, safer controls over memory & search history, adding several new connectors, and hardening sync reliability. Key workflow changes include explicit history-purging behaviour, a new flag to remove search history from the CLI/API, and fixes that make Drive/Asana synchronisation and indexing more robust.

Highlights

  • New forget(clean_history=True) option so you can remove search history without needing other inputs.
  • Users can now delete their own search history via the API and server endpoints.
  • New connectors: Obsidian (vaults), Asana (tasks) and OneNote are added and their syncs are hardened.
  • Reliability improvements: Drive and Asana syncs are faster and resumable; graph and index operations avoid unnecessary work.

Breaking Changes

  • Dataset delete now purges associated search and conversation history: When you delete a dataset, all associated history is removed. Action required: if you depend on preserved search or session traces for backups or audit, export or back them up before deleting datasets.
  • run_info structure changed: run_info metadata no longer contains the full 'data' items that ingestion pipelines previously stored. Action required: any code or tooling that read run_info expecting embedded data must be updated to instead fetch original items via their data ids or use the new storage shapes. A migration to remove the old data shape is included in this release.
  • Fail-on-history-purge: delete/forget operations that attempt to purge history will now fail if the purge cannot be completed. Action required: ensure the service has permission to delete search history and that long-running purge operations are allowed to complete; handle failures when calling delete APIs.
  • Budget/quota errors: Budget exhaustion and payment-required errors are raised more consistently (LLMPaymentRequiredError). Action required: clients should catch and handle these exceptions if they interact with LLM billing paths.

New Features

  • Forget(clean_history=True): A new clean_history flag for the forget command and API that lets you purge recorded search history while keeping other deletion behaviour. What it does: call forget(clean_history=True) to remove stored search history related to a dataset or user. Why it matters: you can now remove traces of user searches without performing other delete operations, making privacy and cleanup operations clearer and easier.
  • Delete your own search history: The server and API now include a route that allows a user to delete their own search history. What it does: end-users (via API or UI) can remove their personal queries and search metadata. Why it matters: improves user privacy and compliance by giving individuals direct control over their search traces.
  • Obsidian connector (vaults): A new connector that ingests Obsidian vaults (local notes and markdown vaults). What it does: lets you import notes stored in Obsidian vaults into Cognee so they become searchable and recallable. Why it matters: broadens supported sources so personal knowledge stored in Obsidian can be included in memory and search workflows.
  • Asana connector: A first-class Asana connector for tasks and events. What it does: syncs Asana tasks and events into Cognee and makes them available for search and recall. Why it matters: teams using Asana can now include task context and history in their memory-driven workflows.
  • OneNote connector: Add OneNote support for ingestion and sync. What it does: pulls OneNote content into Cognee so notebooks are searchable and linked into memory. Why it matters: integrates another major note-taking source so users' OneNote content participates in memory and search.
  • Expose dataset and data ids in recall hits: Recall results now include the dataset (where the hit came from) and underlying data ids. What it does: returned recall hits include the dataset name and the original item id for clarity. Why it matters: makes it easier to trace answers back to source documents for auditing and follow-up.

Improvements

  • Forward clean_history through CogneeClient.forget and name history-only cases clearly so the client and server behaviour match and error messages are clearer.
  • Docs: Clarified what memory_only (memory-only deletion) keeps versus what remains on disk, so users better understand deletion semantics.
  • Search code: reuse internal delete_user_search_history logic, add a dedicated search-history delete route, and scope search history actions to the calling user to avoid accidental cross-user deletion.
  • Graph and indexing: look up graph edges only once per add_edges call and in has_edges to reduce redundant work during graph updates and ingestion.
  • Drive sync: sped up and widened Drive sync and made it more robust to interruptions (name unreadable PDFs, better resume logic).
  • Asana sync: made resumable, improved timestamp handling, and raise on repeated sync tokens to avoid stuck syncs.
  • Index building: retry skipped HNSW index builds on every version change to increase reliability of vector indexes when upgrading.
  • Error handling: surface budget exhaustion and quota/permission errors through shared helpers so client code and calling apps receive consistent, actionable exceptions.

Performance

  • Faster graph updates: avoiding repeated edge lookups reduces CPU during bulk add_edges operations (practical impact: faster ingestion and lower CPU on large graph updates).
  • Faster Drive sync: file syncs run faster and handle wider datasets (practical impact: quicker initial syncs and catch-ups for Google Drive sources).
  • Index retry improvements: HNSW (vector index) build retries are more reliable after version changes, reducing failed index states that block search.

Security

  • Dependency updates: boto3 is now listed in the aws install extra so AWS integrations get a compatible SDK when users install the aws extras. The certifi bundle was updated (require certifi 2026.10.19) and container CA bundles were refreshed to improve TLS reliability.
  • Stricter error propagation for budget/quota failures so callers get explicit payment/quota errors instead of silent retries. This helps avoid leaking unexpected retry behaviour and surfaces required remediation.

Bug Fixes

  • Purge history on every dataset delete so dataset removal no longer leaves stale search or conversation history behind.
  • Forget now fails if history purge fails (so partial deletes won't silently leave traces).
  • Stop storing data items inside run_info (internal pipeline run metadata) — stored run_info now excludes the original 'data' payload to avoid duplication and reduce storage.
  • Stop native adapter retrying quota failures to prevent busy-loop retries on quota errors and return quota errors promptly.
  • Fix: name unreadable Drive PDFs so they are still tracked correctly during sync and ingestion.
  • Fix: resume cut Asana listings and make Asana listing/sync more robust to transient API errors and pagination cuts.
  • Fix: scope tracing spans (observability) to the calling user so telemetry no longer mixes users.
  • Various connector hardenings and test fixes (Drive, OneNote, Gmail, Notion, etc.) to improve real-world ingestion reliability.

Technical Changes

  • Large refactors and many new and updated ingestion connectors added (Google Drive, Gmail, Notion, Obsidian, Asana, OneNote) with new sync code and tests.
  • Added many task modules for code documentation extraction, memify global context index builders, and session distillation pieces used by internal pipelines and examples.
  • CI and tests: split integration jobs, added new API snapshots for the search history delete route, and refreshed test coverage and fixtures.
  • Internal: migrations added/updated (including a migration that drops run_info data fields), numerous refactors to server/client plumbing, and observability/tracing improvements.

Dependency Updates

Added:

  • certifi >=2026.10.19

Compatibility

Component Supported / Required
Python >=3.10,<3.15
pydantic >=2.10.5
litellm >=1.102.2,<2.0.0
fastapi >=0.116.2,<1.0.0
sqlalchemy >=2.0.39,<3.0.0
lancedb >=0.39.0,<0.40.0
ladybug ==0.19.0

— The Cognee Team · 2026-10-23

entry.title: v1.6.5 — Faster trace processing & richer code-graph docs
entry.content:
v1.6.5 — Faster trace processing & richer code-graph docs

Release Date: 2026-10-16
Changes: v1.6.4 → v1.6.5

Pull Requests: #5287, #5534, #5620, #5622, #5720, #5721, #5722, #5725, #5726, #5751, #5798, #5898, #5938, #5955, #5958, #5961

Summary

This release speeds up trace and ingestion pipelines, improves session handling, and makes code documentation searchable inside the code graph. It also adds a new memify API, better embedding compatibility (base64), and several security and connector hardenings.

Highlights

  • Faster trace processing: traces are persisted and processed in fewer, larger operations for lower latency and fewer database writes.
  • Code-graph docstrings: function/class docstrings are stored as graph documents and linked to code symbols for better code recall and search.
  • New Memify API endpoints: convert content into memory entries via the API to make ingestion and downstream recall simpler.
  • Base64 embeddings support: request embeddings encoded as base64 where providers allow it to improve compatibility and reduce transport issues.
  • Security & connectors: daily CVE Slack alert, Google Calendar connector hardening, and improved OAuth/token sharing.

Breaking Changes

  • datamodel-code-generator requirement bumped: if you use a custom graph_model generation step, you must have datamodel-code-generator >= 0.56.0. What to do: upgrade that dependency when generating custom graph models to avoid generation errors.

New Features

  • Store code docstrings in the code graph: Docstrings (the documentation strings attached to functions, classes and modules) are now saved as first-class graph documents and linked to the corresponding code symbols. What it does: when you ingest code, the human-readable docstrings are indexed and connected to the code symbol nodes. Why it matters: search and code-aware agents can return richer, context-aware answers and surface inline documentation alongside code references.
  • New Memify API and endpoints: 'memify' is the process of converting content (files, messages, or other data) into memory entries the system can store and recall. What it does: we added server endpoints and CLI wiring to create memory entries (memify) directly via the API. Why it matters: it simplifies turning raw content into searchable, recallable memories for use in recall and improve flows.
  • Request base64 embeddings where supported: some embedding providers accept embeddings encoded as base64 to avoid binary transport problems. What it does: Cognee will request base64-encoded embedding responses when the provider supports it. Why it matters: improves interoperability with certain providers and reduces problems when sending/receiving binary embedding payloads.
  • Persist a session's trace backlog as one document: traces are the interaction records (events, steps, logs) from a user session. What it does: instead of writing many small trace documents, Cognee can now persist a session's backlog as one consolidated document. Why it matters: fewer database writes and improved throughput for high-traffic sessions, leading to faster ingestion and lower resource usage.
  • Build trace pass windows in a single cognify run: 'cognify' is the pipeline run that converts raw traces into memory entries. What it does: trace windowing for a pass is computed in one cognify execution rather than multiple runs. Why it matters: reduces repeated pipeline runs and speeds up trace processing so results appear faster and more consistently.

Improvements

  • Session/dataset binding reliability and speed: bound sessions (sessions tied to a specific dataset — a collection of documents you've added) now skip unnecessary re-reads and correctly route skill runs to the bound dataset. This reduces latency and fixes several edge cases where a stale or mismatched binding could cause errors.
  • Curation and distillation fixes: distilled entries are sealed per curator batch and new entries are curated by default on each distill run. This makes automated filtering and quality control of memory entries more consistent.
  • Embedding token tracking: the activity model now records embedding token usage so you can see embedding costs per activity.
  • Google and Azure auth sharing: OAuth and token-provider code for Google and Azure have been consolidated so integrations reuse the same adapters, reducing duplication and improving maintenance.
  • Improved content selection for distillation: only the needed QA turns are read during distillation which reduces work and speeds the distill process.

Performance

  • Faster trace ingestion: persisting the session trace backlog as one document and draining the backlog per run reduce database writes and pipeline churn, improving throughput for active sessions.
  • Reduced cognify runs: building trace pass windows and handling them in one run means fewer pipeline invocations and lower end-to-end processing time for trace-to-memory conversion.
  • Lower overhead for embedding transfers: base64 embedding support can reduce transport issues and improve compatibility with some providers, leading to smoother embedding flows.

Security

  • Daily CVE alert to Slack: a new GitHub Actions job sends a daily summary of known CVEs to Slack so maintainers can track vulnerable dependencies.
  • Google Calendar connector hardening and shared OAuth adapter: multiple fixes improve robustness and error handling for Google integrations and centralize OAuth behavior to reduce security risk.
  • Hidden NATURAL_LANGUAGE setting and remediation guidance: a security-sensitive surface has been removed from the public surfaces and a remediation path is set.

Bug Fixes

  • Drain the trace backlog per run: fixed a bug that could leave traces unprocessed across runs.
  • Break loop on payment error: addressed an infinite-loop risk when payment errors occur during an operation.
  • Refuse stale session binding like a forbidden id: stale or invalid session-to-dataset bindings are now rejected consistently, preventing silent misrouting of data.
  • Read only the needed QA turns for distillation: reduces unnecessary reads and potential errors during distillation.
  • Accept string dataset_id on typed entries and route typed entries to the session's dataset: fixes that prevented some entries from being correctly bound to datasets.

Technical Changes

  • Large internal refactors across memify, improve, and cognify pipelines to consolidate task registries, distillation stages, and graph-change operations.
  • New evaluation tooling (Locomo) and many test/CI workflow updates (including new workflows for CVE alerting and latest-libraries checks).
  • Added Azure managed identity support and tightened Litellm client behavior and types.

Dependency Updates

Updated:

  • datamodel-code-generator: >=0.54.0 → >=0.56.0
  • enola-cli: ==0.4.26 → ==0.4.30
  • litellm: >=1.83.7,<1.97.0 → >=1.102.2,<2.0.0

Removed:

  • python-magic-bin <0.5

Compatibility

Python >=3.10,<3.15
pydantic >=2.10.5
litellm >=1.102.2,<2.0.0
fastapi >=0.116.2,<1.0.0
sqlalchemy >=2.0.39,<3.0.0
lancedb >=0.39.0,<0.40.0

entry.title: v1.6.5.dev0 — Distillation, Embeddings & Connector Hardening
entry.content:
v1.6.5.dev0 — Distillation, Embeddings & Connector Hardening

Release Date: 2026-10-16
Changes: v1.6.4.dev0 → v1.6.5.dev0

Pull Requests: #5287, #5534, #5620, #5622, #5720, #5721, #5722, #5725, #5726, #5751, #5798, #5898

Summary

This release focuses on making memory distillation more reliable, improving how embeddings are produced and metered, and hardening connectors and LLM integrations. It includes several bug fixes, security and operational improvements, and a few breaking changes related to legacy embedding surfaces and local cache layout.

Highlights

  • More reliable distillation: distillation now reads only the QA turns it needs, seals entries per curator batch, and curates every new entry by default so distilled memories are accurate and consistent.
  • Embeddings improvements: support requesting base64-encoded embeddings where supported, meter embedding token usage, lower the default embedding batch size for stability, and keep local model cache under a predictable path.
  • Connector and LLM fixes: Gmail and Google Calendar connectors were hardened (better quota handling and permissions), litellm and Mistral model handling were improved, and Azure token handling is shared to reduce auth complexity.
  • Security & alerts: daily CVE alert delivery to Slack was added and repository security docs updated to help teams stay informed.

Breaking Changes

  • Triplet embedding / triplet memify surfaces removed or deprecated — the older triplet embedding surfaces have been deprecated and parts removed. If you rely on 'triplet' embedding flows, migrate to the newer embedding surfaces and memify pipelines. Check your pipelines and replacements before upgrading.
  • datamodel-code-generator minimum version raised — custom graph model generation requires datamodel-code-generator >= 0.56.0. Upgrade this dependency if you use custom graph models.
  • Fastembed cache path change — FASTEMBED_CACHE_PATH was removed from the .env.template and fastembed now uses ~/.cognee/models by default. If you relied on a custom FASTEMBED_CACHE_PATH, update your environment or move your cache to the new location.

New Features

  • Request Base64 embeddings where supported — Some embedding providers can return vectors encoded as base64. Cognee now requests base64 embeddings when the provider supports them. Why it matters: base64 can improve compatibility with certain providers and transports, reducing encoding errors and simplifying integrations.
  • Daily CVE alert to Slack — A new automated alert posts daily security advisories (CVE summaries) to a configured Slack channel. Why it matters: keeps your team aware of new vulnerabilities affecting dependencies so you can act faster.
  • Clone a chosen branch of a repo during ingestion — You can now select which branch to clone when pulling a repository. Why it matters: makes ingestion reproducible and lets you index branch-specific code or docs without manual repo handling.
  • Embedding token usage metering — The system now records the number of embedding tokens used per activity. Why it matters: helps understand and audit embedding usage for cost tracking and debugging.

Improvements

  • More focused distillation: distillation now reads only the required QA turns (instead of whole conversations), and curator runs seal distilled entries per batch so partial results don’t leak. This reduces work and makes distilled summaries more deterministic.
  • Curate every new entry per distill run by default — every newly added memory entry is considered for distillation unless you change the setting, making sure new content is summarized promptly.
  • Bind typed entries to the session's dataset — when the system writes typed (structured) memory entries during a session, they are now correctly associated with that session's dataset. Why it matters: preserves correct dataset ownership and prevents data from landing in the wrong dataset.
  • Take dataset_id on remember_skill_run_entry — explicit dataset routing for remembered skill outputs improves traceability and correctness.
  • Fastembed and local model cache changes — fastembed models are now kept under ~/.cognee/models by default for consistent caching across platforms; the ENV template no longer exposes a deprecated FASTEMBED_CACHE_PATH. Why it matters: fewer surprises when loading local models and better cross-machine behavior.
  • Lower default embedding batch size (36 → 32) — reduces memory spikes and improves stability on constrained machines.
  • Return plain vectors from embed_text — embedding functions now return raw numeric vectors rather than wrapped objects in more places, simplifying downstream use.

Performance

  • More stable embedding usage: lowering the default embedding batch size and keeping models in a consistent local cache reduces memory and latency spikes when creating embeddings.
  • Reduced unnecessary distillation work: reading only necessary QA turns and sealing per batch reduces I/O and CPU used during distillation runs.
  • Shared counters and pacing: connectors and background pollers share counts and pacing logic where appropriate to avoid accidental overload and smoothing throughput.

Security

  • Daily CVE alert to Slack — daily summaries of dependency vulnerabilities are now available via a new GitHub Actions + Slack flow to help teams respond faster.
  • Hide NATURAL_LANGUAGE surface and remediation guidance — certain surfaces were made less visible and remediation notes were added to help secure deployments.
  • Azure token provider sharing — Azure token usage is centralized for fewer spurious credential refreshes and simpler secure handling.
  • Google Calendar and Gmail hardening — the calendar connector now has stricter checks; Gmail is more resilient to per-user quota rejections and shares pacing across mailbox processing to avoid accidental rate-limit spikes.

Bug Fixes

  • Read only the needed QA turns for distillation so the distillation step no longer loads unnecessary conversation turns.
  • Drain the agent trace backlog per improve run so new improve runs don't see stale traces.
  • Seal distilled entries per curator batch to avoid partial distillations being visible.
  • Curate every new entry per distill run by default to ensure fresh content gets summarized.
  • Pin Data selection reads under the lock to avoid races with concurrent deletes/forgets.
  • Fix visualize permission checks so the permission-skip option is applied only when explicitly requested, and skip the permission check only for the dataset owner when appropriate.
  • Survive Gmail per-user quota rejections and share pacing per mailbox to reduce operation failures.
  • Return 403 with a clear message when Cypher (graph DB query interface) is disabled, instead of a generic error.
  • Narrow litellm response types and correctly return Mistral’s parsed model representation to improve LLM reliability and type safety.

Technical Changes

  • Large refactor of retrieval and code search components — new modules for broad retriever, code retriever and hybrid retrieval were added or reorganized to improve search quality and maintainability.
  • Memify pipelines reorganized — memify and related task registration were refactored; some old task modules (triplet embedding) were removed as part of the SDK cleanup.
  • New evaluation framework assets — a Locomo-based evaluation adapter, metrics, and many reference run artifacts were added for internal evaluation and end-to-end QA.
  • Improvements to LLM adapters and token/encoding utilities — better litellm adapters, Azure identity handling, and embedding encoding utilities to improve compatibility across LLM/back-end providers.
  • Session and data selection robustness — session management and data selection logic were tightened (locking and selection checks) to avoid races with forget/delete workflows.

Dependency Updates

Updated:

  • datamodel-code-generator: >=0.54.0 → >=0.56.0
  • enola-cli: ==0.4.26 → ==0.4.30
  • litellm: >=1.83.7,<1.97.0 → >=1.102.2,<2.0.0

Removed:

  • python-magic-bin <0.5

entry.title: v1.6.4 — Vector storage & DB reliability fixes
entry.content:
v1.6.4 — Vector storage & DB reliability fixes

Release Date: 2026-10-13
Changes: v1.6.3 → v1.6.4

Summary

This patch release fixes several backend issues around vector search adapters and the Turso database adapter, and removes an unwanted background pruning task for LanceDB-backed stores. The changes reduce memory use and errors during searches, make Turso open failures report consistently, and add tests and harness fixes to improve reliability.

Highlights

  • Avoid returning the raw vector column during searches for LanceDB and pgvector adapters — reduces memory use and prevents failures.
  • Turso errors raised during database open now surface as OperationalError so calling code can handle them consistently.
  • Removed LanceDB background pruning to stop unexpected background work that could interfere with searches.
  • Added tests and harness fixes to prevent intermittent subprocess/session failures and improve stability.

Breaking Changes

  • Behavior change for LanceDB-backed datasets: automatic background pruning has been removed. If you relied on automatic pruning/compaction to reclaim storage space, you may need to run compaction or pruning manually (via LanceDB tooling or your existing maintenance processes). This is a behavioral change rather than an API incompatibility, but it may affect disk usage and maintenance procedures.

New Features

  • No new end-user features in this release — this update focuses on bug fixes and reliability improvements.

Improvements

  • LanceDB adapter: stopped selecting (returning) the raw vector column when performing vector searches. The vector column contains the numeric embedding for each item; excluding it from search results reduces network and memory usage and avoids returning large binary data that consuming code doesn't need during search.
  • pgvector adapter: same change as above for PostgreSQL pgvector-backed datasets — searches no longer select the raw vector column, yielding the same memory and stability benefits.
  • Turso dialect (database adapter): when opening a Turso database fails due to an I/O or underlying client error, Cognee now raises a SQLAlchemy OperationalError (a standard, catchable database error). This makes error handling consistent across database backends and lets calling code react to open failures reliably.
  • Removed LanceDB background prunes: automatic background pruning tasks inside LanceDB-backed storage were removed to prevent unexpected background activity that could interfere with queries or tests. This reduces surprising concurrent work during searches and testing.

Performance

  • Search queries against LanceDB and pgvector should use less memory and run with lower latency because the large vector column is no longer fetched unless explicitly requested.
  • Reduced intermittent test/flakiness from subprocess/session failures thanks to harness fixes and added tests.

Security

  • No security vulnerabilities or credential changes in this release.

Bug Fixes

  • Fixed harness issues and added tests to cover subprocess/session failure scenarios, reducing intermittent CI/test failures.
  • Fixed LanceDB and pgvector adapters to stop selecting the vector column during search (prevents large binary data from being returned and reduces memory/serialization errors).
  • Raised Turso 'open' errors as OperationalError to avoid exposing low-level client exceptions directly to callers.
  • Removed LanceDB background pruning logic that could run during operations and cause unexpected interference.

Technical Changes

  • Cognee-MCP version bumped to 0.5.7 and lockfile updates synced to cognee 1.6.3 in the cognee-mcp/uv.lock file.
  • Dependency upgrades in the lockfile include newer lancedb, lance-namespace, and pylance package versions.
  • Various lockfile and packaging metadata updates (pyproject and uv.lock) were applied.
  • Repository housekeeping: commit-author verification added and release chore commits for v1.6.4.

Compatibility

Component Supported / Required
Python >=3.10,<3.15
pydantic >=2.10.5
litellm >=1.83.7,<1.97.0
fastapi >=0.116.2,<1.0.0
sqlalchemy >=2.0.39,<3.0.0
lancedb >=0.39.0,<0.40.0
ladybug ==0.19.0

— The Cognee Team · 2026-10-13

entry.title: v1.6.4.dev0 — Vector search reliability & Turso error handling
entry.content:
v1.6.4.dev0 — Vector search reliability & Turso error handling

Release Date: 2026-10-13
Changes: v1.6.3 → v1.6.4.dev0

Pull Requests: #5745

Summary

This small development release fixes a key vector-search bug and improves Turso database error handling. It also updates a few packaging dependencies and tests so search is more reliable and errors are handled consistently.

Highlights

  • Fixed a vector-search bug that prevented selecting raw vector data during search (pgvector and Lancedb adapters) — reduces bandwidth and avoids errors.
  • Turso adapter now raises OperationalError for file/open problems so callers and ORMs handle them consistently.
  • Dependency and packaging updates: cognee-mcp bumped, lancedb and related packages upgraded in the lockfile.
  • Improved and added tests around vector distance semantics and shared Turso behavior.

Improvements

  • PGVector and Lancedb adapters (the pieces that talk to Postgres+pgvector and Lancedb vector stores) no longer ask the database to return the full raw vector column during a similarity search. This means searches return only the metadata and nearest-neighbor scores, which reduces network payload, avoids size or serialization errors, and makes search responses faster and more reliable.
  • Turso database dialect now converts low-level file/open errors (pyturso IoError) into SQLAlchemy's OperationalError. In plain terms: when Turso can't open or access its data files, Cognee will raise a standard database OperationalError instead of an obscure raw exception. That makes error handling predictable for applications and tooling that expect DBAPI-style errors.

Performance

  • Reduced data transfer during vector searches by not returning full vector columns; practical result: lower memory usage and faster search responses for large vectors.

Bug Fixes

  • SDK-1096 — Fixed an issue where search queries selected the raw vector column in pgvector and Lancedb adapters. Selecting the raw vector could cause oversized responses or trigger serialization problems; the adapters now exclude the vector column from the selected fields during search.
  • Turso open errors now surfaced as OperationalError instead of a raw IoError, preventing unexpected exception types from bubbling up to callers.

Technical Changes

  • Bumped cognee-mcp package version to 0.5.7 and synced lock files with cognee 1.6.3. This is a packaging/lockfile change for the MCP server distribution.
  • Lockfile upgrades: lancedb updated (to 0.39.0), lance-namespace and lance-namespace-urllib3-client updated (to 0.11.1), pylance updated (to 12.0.0), and dateparser was added as a dependency entry in the lockfile. These updates bring newer native wheels and bugfixes for underlying vector-store libraries.
  • Tests updated/added: vector distance semantics tests and shared Turso tests were added/adjusted to validate the fixes.

entry.title: v1.6.3 — Better Temporal Search & Retrieval Accuracy
entry.content:
v1.6.3 — Better Temporal Search & Retrieval Accuracy

Release Date: 2026-10-07
Changes: v1.6.2 → v1.6.3

Pull Requests: #4116, #5225, #5226, #5249, #5275, #5277, #5309, #5320, #5361, #5428, #5434

Summary

This release sharpens Cognee's search and ingestion reliability: temporal queries are more precise and inclusive, natural-language searches return matching rows and skip irrelevant turn analysis, and ingestion validators prevent malformed data. Several operational fixes improve container builds and external integrations.

Highlights

  • Temporal search windows now include their boundary dates and rank date matches more accurately.
  • Natural-language searches return matching database rows in the response payload and skip 'turn analysis' to avoid unrelated context.
  • Stronger ingestion validation rejects malformed node sets and fixes Notion block rendering (no depth caps).
  • Agents restrictions tightened: agents can no longer create nested agents; parent/agent dataset access behavior corrected.
  • Operational fixes: Docker images now include git and a DLT dependency is pinned to avoid import failures.

Breaking Changes

  • DLT dependency pinned below 1.31: The DLT package used for some ingestion paths is now pinned to versions older than 1.31 to avoid import errors. Action: if you manage your own environment, pin DLT to <1.31 or update your dependency constraints until a newer Cognee release lifts this pin.
  • Removed temporal_cognify option: The temporal_cognify configuration option was removed. Action: remove any temporal_cognify references from your configuration or code.
  • create_agent refuses nested agents and agents cannot create agents: Nested agents are no longer allowed and once created, agents cannot create other agents. Action: update any automation or scripts that relied on creating nested agents.
  • Public sign-up no longer accepts a parent: The signup flow will reject attempts to set a parent account during public sign-ups. Action: remove parent-setting from public signup flows or handle linking after signup.

New Features

  • Natural-language search returns row matches in the payload: When you run a natural-language search (a search using plain sentences), Cognee now includes any matching table rows in the response payload. This makes it easier to programmatically access the exact rows that matched the query instead of only high-level text answers.
  • Inclusive temporal windows: 'since X' and 'until X' queries now include X in the query window. If you ask for events 'since 2023-01-01' or 'until 2023-01-31', results on those exact boundary dates are now included, giving you predictable behavior for date ranges.
  • Notion ingestion removes depth caps and avoids recursive rendering: Notion pages and blocks are now rendered without an artificial depth limit and the Notion renderer avoids recursive expansion. That means deeper or more complex Notion pages ingest more faithfully and without runaway recursion.
  • DLT ingestion options grouped as dlt_config and temporal_columns restored: The ingestion configuration for DLT sources (a data-transfer tool used to bring tabular data in) is better organized under a single dlt_config section, and the option to select temporal columns (date/time columns) is restored so you can control which columns feed time-sensitive searches.

Improvements

  • Temporal ranking and candidate widening: Date anchors (pieces of content tagged with dates) are ranked by how tightly they match your time window, and Cognee widens the pool of temporal candidates so relevant items near the window edges are more likely to be found. Practically, this makes time-based queries return more relevant items and rank the closest matches higher.
  • Natural-language search skips turn analysis: Natural-language searches no longer run 'turn analysis' (analysis that tries to stitch together conversational turns), which reduces noise from unrelated conversational context and leads to cleaner, more relevant results.
  • Cleaner logs and privacy: The internal 'extraction reason' (why a piece of content was extracted) is removed from logs to keep logs focused and avoid exposing internal reasoning steps.
  • Stronger node_set handling when ingesting rows: The system now refuses malformed node_set values (for example, where a row's node_set is not a JSON list) and rejects bad entries inside node_set lists. This prevents bad ingestion data from corrupting downstream indexing or visualizations.
  • Agent and dataset access behavior clarified: Parent accounts correctly reach their agents' datasets, and listing/lookup of agents now correctly limits results to a user's own agents. This makes permissions and dataset visibility more consistent.

Performance

  • Search candidate selection widened for temporal queries: Broader candidate selection improves recall for time-sensitive searches, especially when relevant items sit just outside a strict window. This may slightly increase search work for higher recall but yields more useful results.

Security

  • Extraction reasons removed from logs to avoid leaking internal extraction rationale.
  • Sign-up protection: public sign-up no longer accepts a 'parent' account during creation, preventing accidental or unauthorized linking of accounts at signup.

Bug Fixes

  • Return natural-language search rows through payload: Fixed an issue where natural-language queries did not include matching rows in responses.
  • Make 'until X' and 'since X' include X: Fixed off-by-one behavior in temporal windows so boundary dates are included.
  • Rank dates relative to the time window and log missing windows: Fixed ranking so dates are scored relative to the requested window and added a log when a time window is missing to aid debugging.
  • Render Notion blocks without recursive expansion and remove depth caps: Fixed broken or incomplete Notion ingestion where deep nesting could be truncated or cause recursion.
  • Refuse malformed node_set and validate entries: Fixed multiple bugs that allowed malformed node_set values or invalid entries — ingestion now fails loudly for malformed input so issues are caught early.
  • Stop agents from creating other agents and refuse nested agents at creation: Fixed agent creation so agents cannot create further agents and top-level agent creation enforces non-nested structure.
  • Stop warning when a chunk has no summary: Removed noisy warnings when content chunks legitimately lack a summary.
  • Make Chinese queries trigger the skill gate: Fixed the recall gate so it fires correctly on Chinese-language queries.
  • Install git in Docker images and keep Cypher search raw: Docker images now have git available (fixes build and runtime scripts) and Cypher-based search results retain their raw form where required.
  • Pin dlt below 1.31 to keep importable: Avoids a runtime import error by restricting the DLT dependency to a compatible range.
  • Various CI and test fixes: Multiple workflow and test updates to keep CI stable (label workflow, PR message requirement, test cleanups).
  • Better error handling across pipelines and adapters: Several fixes to avoid swallowed type errors and preserve installer error messages.

Technical Changes

  • Large refactors and new adapters: Significant internal refactors and new/updated adapters for Turso (a hosted database), LanceDB and Lancedb-related processes, and vector store components. These are internal plumbing changes to improve scalability and maintainability.
  • Pipelines and hooks: After-run hooks in pipeline code now propagate errors instead of silently swallowing them; pipeline task execution code was refactored for clarity and robustness.
  • Telemetry and CI adjustments: Updated telemetry scripts and many GitHub workflow files to improve CI reliability and telemetry aggregation.
  • Visualizer and graph internals: Node set handling and visualizer stages were refactored to keep node sets out of specific visualizer stages and to simplify marker usage.
  • Misc internal: new timestamp parsing utilities, temporal hint helpers, and improved recovery and estimator code for the cognify process.

Dependency Updates

Added:

  • dateparser >=1.2,<2

Updated:

  • dlt: >=1.9.0,<2 → >=1.9.0,<1.31
  • lancedb: >=0.24.3,<1.0.0 → >=0.39.0,<0.40.0
  • pylance: >=0.22.0,<=0.36.0 → >=12.0.0,<12.1.0

Compatibility

Component Supported / Required
Python >=3.10,<3.15
pydantic >=2.10.5
litellm >=1.83.7,<1.97.0
fastapi >=0.116.2,<1.0.0
sqlalchemy >=2.0.39,<3.0.0
lancedb >=0.39.0,<0.40.0
ladybug ==0.19.0

— The Cognee Team · 2026-10-07

entry.title: v1.6.2 — Embedding reliability & Slack history
entry.content:
v1.6.2 — Embedding reliability & Slack history

Release Date: 2026-09-29
Changes: v1.6.1 → v1.6.2

Pull Requests: #4932, #4951, #5146, #5196, #5231, #5235, #5236, #5240, #5241, #5242, #5247, #5250, #5251, #5274

Summary

This release focuses on making embeddings reliable and transparent (no more silent truncation), adds Slack conversation import and sync, and reorganizes how 'skills' are stored for better cross-platform tooling. You'll see clearer errors when embedding fails, safer chunk sizing based on model token limits, and updated CLI/docs to match these behaviors.

Highlights

  • Embedding fixes prevent silent truncation and size chunks by each model's token limit so your content is embedded intact and consistently.
  • Slack integration: import and continuously sync conversation history from Slack into Cognee.
  • Skills moved to a new .agents/skills location with Windows linking support and recovery when linking fails.
  • Better errors and faster failure on unrecoverable embedding errors — you’ll see real causes instead of opaque messages.
  • CLI and docs refreshed (including database migration/commands and Docker quickstart auth fixes).

Breaking Changes

  • Skills path change: Built-in and packaged skills are now under .agents/skills (moved from earlier locations). If you maintain custom scripts, automation, build hooks, or CI that reference the old paths, update them to .agents/skills. A small helper script (link-skills.sh) and a Windows hook were added to assist linking.
  • env_file removed from settings: The runtime setting that automatically loaded an env_file was removed. If you relied on that behavior to load environment variables via the settings file, switch to an explicit env loader in your start scripts or use the newly added shared/env_file helper (see docs/tests for examples).

New Features

  • Slack conversation import and sync — A new integration to import and keep Slack conversation history in sync with Cognee. This pulls channel and thread messages into your datasets so search and memory features can use Slack content. Why it matters: you can build memories, search, and summaries from historical Slack data without manual export.
  • Chunks sized by model input limit — The system now measures each embedding model's input limit (the maximum number of tokens a model accepts) and splits text into chunks sized to that limit. What it does: chunking no longer relies on a fixed heuristic; it respects the actual model/tokenizer limits to avoid unexpected truncation. Why it matters: search and memory will be more complete and consistent because documents are not silently shortened when sent to an embedding model.
  • Skills directory reorganization (.agents) and Windows link hook — Skills (automated agent scripts and examples) are moved from older locations into a new .agents/skills directory and a Windows-friendly hook was added for linking. What it does: standardizes where built-in skills live and makes the linking process work on Windows. Why it matters: easier, more consistent workflows for installing, linking, and running skills across platforms.

Improvements

  • Robust embedding input limit resolution — The SDK now resolves a model's input limit even when optional tokenizer libraries (like transformers) are not installed, and does so asynchronously where appropriate. This reduces startup surprises and improves behavior for lightweight installs.
  • Accurate token counting across tokenizers — Token counts now use each provider's tokenizers (including HuggingFace tokenizers when available), and the model's own special tokens are included in counts. What it does: improves chunk sizing and prevents off-by-a-few-token truncation.
  • Fastembed batch padding — Batches sent to the fast embedding backend are now padded to the longest text in the batch to avoid inconsistent batch-level truncation. Result: fewer silent truncations and more predictable embeddings when sending mixed-length inputs.
  • Clearer embedding errors and fail-fast behavior — Embedding failures now show the underlying cause (not just a generic message) and terminal errors stop retries quickly. Why it matters: you can debug and recover faster when an external provider or configuration is wrong.
  • Recover skill links on failure and validate links without keys — The linking process for skills is more robust: partial failures try to recover links and the link-checking workflow can run without a secret key. This reduces brittle operations and makes CI checks simpler.
  • CLI docs and behavior updates — The CLI documentation has been expanded and clarified (database migration commands, new examples, memory commands notes). The Docker quickstart 401 trap has been improved so the quickstart behaves correctly when auth is missing.

Performance

  • More reliable embedding throughput — By padding fastembed batches and sizing chunks to the model input limits, embeddings avoid silent truncation that used to reduce effective throughput/quality. This improves the practical throughput of usable embeddings for mixed-length inputs.
  • Faster detection of embedding limits in lightweight setups — Input limit resolution now works without heavyweight tokenizer dependencies and resolves asynchronously, reducing delays during embedding initialization.

Security

  • Docker quickstart 401 handling — The Docker quickstart and related docs were fixed to avoid a confusing 401 trap and now produce clearer authentication guidance.

Bug Fixes

  • Marked optional transformers imports correctly for type checking so optional dependencies behave cleanly during installs.
  • Counted HuggingFace tokens correctly using tokenizers (avoids miscounting when different tokenizer code paths are used).
  • Read a model's input limit even when transformers is not installed, preventing silent fallbacks that caused wrong chunk sizes.
  • Ignored previously-saved truncation/padding metadata that could corrupt future chunk sizing decisions.
  • Recovered skill links when clearing fails (link recovery to avoid broken skill installations).
  • Dropped an env_file setting from runtime settings to avoid surprising behavior (see Breaking changes).
  • Logged full tracebacks on delegated CLI command failures so errors are easier to diagnose.
  • Changed the order in which databases are pruned to fix an edge-case deletion ordering bug.

Technical Changes

  • Refactored embedding input_limit() into the engine interface and kept each limit lookup with its provider to make limit resolution pluggable.
  • Dropped a no-op re-raise in fastembed and simplified retry predicate classification to handle missing embedding SDKs cleanly.
  • Refactored tokenizer ordering guards (removed transformers-before-torch guard) and added guarded tests to prevent regressions in import order and padding behavior.
  • Large suite of tests and example additions: many end-to-end, unit, and journey tests were added or expanded (embedding limits, slack history, chunking, journeys), plus a new company_brain multi-source demo and expanded CI workflows.
  • Documentation and skills: numerous documentation updates (AGENTS.md, skills docs, migration guidance, README alignment) and formatting fixes for Python skill examples.

Dependency Updates

Updated:

  • enola-cli: ==0.4.21 → ==0.4.26

Compatibility

Component Supported / Required
Python >=3.10,<3.15
pydantic >=2.10.5
litellm >=1.83.7,<1.97.0
fastapi >=0.116.2,<1.0.0
sqlalchemy >=2.0.39,<3.0.0
lancedb >=0.24.3,<1.0.0
ladybug ==0.19.0

— The Cognee Team · 2026-09-29

entry.title: v1.6.1 — Google Sync & Visualization
entry.content:
v1.6.1 — Google Sync & Visualization

Release Date: 2026-09-24
Changes: v1.6.0 → v1.6.1

Pull Requests: #5141, #5158, #5166, #5180

Summary

This release strengthens Google integrations (Drive and Gmail), improves visualization streaming for large subgraphs, and smooths up GLiNER installation and telemetry. It also adds better provenance scoping, stamps external metadata onto document chunks so retrieval returns richer results, and fixes a range of sync, ingestion and UI issues.

Highlights

  • New Google Drive OAuth connector plus Gmail and shared-drive sync — easier, safer import from Google workspaces.
  • Streaming /visualize/json responses in chunks so large graph views load without exhausting memory.
  • GLiNER installer overhauled: installs off the event loop, auto-installs CPU Torch on first use, and reports install telemetry and errors.
  • Chunks now carry document external metadata and that metadata is surfaced in hybrid retrieval (combined semantic+lexical search).

Breaking Changes

  • dlt is now a core dependency: The CSV loader no longer gates imports on dlt; dlt has been promoted to a core dependency. If you install Cognee from source or manage dependencies manually, ensure dlt is available in your environment or will be installed by your package manager.

New Features

  • Google Drive OAuth connector: Adds a full OAuth-based connector for Google Drive that lets you authorize and sync files from your Google account or shared drives. Why it matters: simplifies securely ingesting Drive content into Cognee and supports shared-drive workflows.
  • Gmail and shared Google sync: Adds Gmail ingestion and shared-drive sync support, plus UI and progress indicators for Google sync operations. What it does: lets you connect Gmail and monitor sync progress in the UI; why it matters: more seamless ingestion from Gmail and clearer sync status.
  • Bundled Google connectors in SDK: Google-related connectors are now included in the SDK distribution. What it does: reduces extra install steps and mismatched versions; why it matters: faster setup and fewer integration errors.
  • Stream /visualize/json in chunks: Large visualization responses (graph/subgraph JSON) are now streamed in chunked pieces instead of one big payload. What it does: avoids high memory usage and enables viewing large graphs; why it matters: visualization of big memory graphs is more reliable and responsive.
  • GLiNER installer improvements: The GLiNER named-entity model installer now runs off the server event loop, records telemetry for installs and errors, and recommends required extras when install fails. Why it matters: avoids blocking the server, gives clearer error messages, and improves first-time setup.
  • CPU Torch on first use for GLiNER: When GLiNER needs Torch (PyTorch), the CPU build is installed on first use rather than forcing it at package install. What it does: defers heavy installs until necessary; why it matters: reduces initial install friction for users who don't need GLiNER right away.
  • Document external_metadata stamped on chunks and surfaced in hybrid retrieval: When documents are split into chunks, external metadata you provide (for example, original file path or source ID) is now preserved on each chunk and included in hybrid search results (hybrid = semantic + keyword search). Why it matters: search results include richer context and make it easier to link a result back to its original document.

Improvements

  • Hardened Google Drive sync and OAuth binding: Several fixes make the Drive sync process more robust, reduce race conditions, and preserve credential metadata across reconnects. Why it matters: safer, more reliable sync and fewer lost credentials.
  • Defer orphan cleanup until ingestion success is confirmed: Cleanup of temporary/orphaned records that could occur during ingestion is now delayed until the ingestion is confirmed successful. Why it matters: prevents accidental deletion of items when ingest processes fail or are retried.
  • Rank and show context for source-check hits: When scanning docs for issues, results are now ranked and include surrounding context. Why it matters: makes triage and diagnostics faster and more actionable.
  • Refined provenance scoping: Provenance (who/what produced a piece of data) is now correctly scoped to the caller’s readable datasets, preventing leakage of dataset-level orientation data. Why it matters: stronger data isolation and clearer provenance outputs.
  • Better HTTP error for undecodable files: The CSV loader now returns HTTP 415 (unsupported media type) for undecodable files instead of a 500 server error. Why it matters: clearer error semantics for users and callers.
  • Observability: GenAI embedding spans now include standard attributes so tracing and observability tools get consistent data for embedding operations.

Performance

  • Visualization streaming: Chunked /visualize/json reduces peak memory usage and allows rendering of much larger graph snapshots without exhausting server memory.
  • GLiNER install moved off event loop: Installing GLiNER components no longer blocks the main event loop, improving responsiveness during first-time setup.
  • Bundling Google connectors in SDK reduces client-side installation friction and can speed up getting integrations running.

Security

  • Hardening around Google Drive sync and OAuth binding to reduce race conditions and preserve credential metadata on reconnects, decreasing the chance of sync failures or lost credentials.
  • Potential CodeQL cookie-construction finding addressed (construction using user-supplied input) — reduces risk flagged by static analysis.
  • Access and provenance scope tightened so callers only see provenance for datasets they can read; this reduces accidental data exposure.

Bug Fixes

  • Pin the correct distribution for GLiNER Python imports to avoid a shadowed import causing runtime errors.
  • Order GLiNER install telemetry and register errors so failures are visible in diagnostics.
  • Recommend the gliner extra when GLiNER-related installs fail to give clearer fix guidance.
  • Resolve entity type resolution in bounded graph reads so visualization and graph queries return correct entity labels.
  • Fix dataset pagination, ordering and deduplication issues across clients and CI, so dataset lists and pages behave consistently.
  • Keep PR text out of docs-sync shell steps, and correctly compute docs paths from checked pages to avoid doc-sync regressions.
  • Fix various Google sync and integration CI regressions and make Google sync cleanup safe.
  • Drop duplicate rewriting in self-improvement module and expose control for remember self-improvement.

Technical Changes

  • New/rewritten visualization modules and graph stream implementation to support streaming JSON and bounded neighborhood reads.
  • Bounded neighborhood reads implemented in SQL for graph databases to limit subgraph sizes and avoid heavy queries.
  • Large number of new tests and CI workflows added (visualization, Google integrations, graph/neighborhood contract helpers, docs triage automation).
  • New task implementations and docs for Google Drive and Gmail connectors, plus example guides and a temporal hybrid cognify demo.

Dependency Updates

Added:

  • dlt >=1.9.0,<2
  • huggingface-hub >=0.34,<1
  • packaging >=24.0
  • pandas >=2.2.2,<3.0.0
  • tokenizers >=0.22,<=0.23.0
